title: Jazz bands in New York in the mid-1920s
summary: Ashcraft recalls the Ramblers and the dominance of records and big bands over small groups.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, I think it was with Nichols on a few occasions. Yes. Every time. Do you remember who the jazz bands were in New York when you arrived there? There were big bands and there were small bands, weren't there, around New York? 25.
The Ramblers, I suppose, were still going, or just barely. That must have been on there or not.
Oh, they went on for a long time under one name or another. But it was pretty much the same nucleus, the Rolini lead.
There was an awful lot of money to be had in making records and also in big bands. And the result was that I don't remember any small bands offhand. Mainly.
What we would have said was huge at that point. 12 would be a great big band.
And so a band that size would depend to a great extent on arrangement. Oh, yes. Rather than the jazz improvisation.
